DISCOVERY 302, PLAINTIFFS GEORGE MANDE AND RAQUEL FERRER'S RE-NOTICE OF MOTION FOR ORDER COMPELLING RESPONDENT BOARD OF REGISTERED NURSING TO RESPOND TO PETITIONERS SPECIAL INTERROGATORIES IS DENIED. PETITIONERS FAILED TO SUBMIT A SEPARATE STATEMENT OF OBJECTIONS, AS REQUIRED UNDER CRC 3.1345(C). PETITIONERS ALSO HAVE NOT SHOWN HOW THE INFORMATION SOUGHT IS REASONABLY CALCULATED TO LEAD TO THE DISCOVERY OF ADMISSIBLE EVIDENCE IN LIGHT OF CCP 1094.5. MOREOVER, MOST IF NOT ALL OF THE SPECIAL INTERROGATORIES RELATE TO PETITIONER MANDE AND, ON APRIL 18, 2016, AFTER THE INSTANT MOTION WAS FILED, THE COURT SUSTAINED A DEMURRER MR. MANDE'S PETITION FOR WRIT OF MANDATE WITHOUT LEAVE TO AMEND. ORDER SIGNED IN OPEN COURT. JUDGE PRO TEM: AARON MINNIS, CLERK: CYNTHIA HERBERT; NOT REPORTED. =302/JPT

LAW AND MOTION 302, RESPONDENT BOARD OF REGISTERED NURSING'S DEMURRER TO THE FIRST AMENDED PETITION FOR WRIT OF ADMINISTRATIVE MANDATE AS TO PETITIONER RAQUEL TOLENTINO ONLY IS SUSTAINED WITHOUT LEAVE TO AMEND. LEAVE TO AMEND IS DENIED BECAUSE IT DOES NOT APPEAR THAT PETITIONER CAN ALLEGE ANY FACTS THAT STATE A LEGALLY COGNIZABLE CLAIM THAT THE DISCIPLINE IMPOSED AGAINST HER MUST BE SET ASIDE. ORDER SIGNED IN OPEN COURT. JUDGE: HAROLD KAHN. CLERK: ROSIE NOGUERA. REPORTER: SHERRY SAWYER, CSR #5976. (302/HK)

LAW AND MOTION 302, RESPONDENT BOARD OF REGISTERED NURSING'S DEMURRER TO PETITION FOR WRIT OF MANDATE IS OVERRULED IN ITS ENTIRETY WITHOUT PREJUDICE. RESPONDENT'S REPLY BRIEF CONCEDES THAT PETITIONER FERRER'S PETITION IS TIMELY. WITH REGARD TO PETITIONER MANDE, THE COURT CANNOT DETERMINE WHETHER HIS PETITION IS ALSO TIMELY. RESPONDENT IS RAISING FACTUAL ISSUES THAT ARE OUTSIDE THE FOUR CORNERS OF THE PETITION. THE PETITION DOES NOT FACIALLY DISCLOSE THAT MR. MANDE'S ACTION IS TIME BARRED AND RESPONDENT NEEDS TO PRESENT EVIDENCE TO ESTABLISH THE STATUTE OF LIMITATIONS DEFENSE. COUNSEL FOR THE DEFENDANT IS TO PROVIDE A FORM OF ORDER AND COMPLY WITH CRC 3.1312. JUDGE: ERNEST GOLDSMITH. CLERK: ROSIE NOGUERA. REPORTER: SHERRY SAWYER, CSR #5976. (302/EG)
